summary: Source-anchored research for MongoDB Drivers. Run status: COMPLETED.

facts.text: Reuse a Node.js MongoClient across operations within a process: it owns a pool for each server in the topology, so creating clients per request creates additional pool infrastructure. (low confidence)

The retryable-writes specification distinguishes retry budgets: without client-side operation timeout (CSOT), one retry is attempted; with CSOT, retries may continue until success, a non-retryable error, or the operation deadline. This is a specification rule, not proof that every released driver implements it. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-27)

In the C# collection bulk-write API, ordered execution stops attempting later operations after an error. Unordered execution attempts all operations and reports write errors afterward. Choose ordering according to operation dependencies and inspect errors for partial completion. (low confidence)

Mongoose buffers model operations before a connection exists, which can resemble a driver hang. Its bufferCommands setting controls this ODM behavior; initial connection rejection and subsequent disconnection also require different error handling. Do not attribute these wrapper behaviors to every native driver. (low confidence)

Spring Boot issue 50925 and Elastic APM issue 4541 traced MongoDB monitor-thread NoClassDefFoundError for InternalStreamConnection to the APM agent closing a shared cached JarFile. Both threads identify Elastic APM 1.57.0 as containing the fix. This documented startup failure does not establish a MongoDB driver defect. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-09-08)

A pool connection handles one request/response at a time. Slow operations can occupy sockets and delay faster operations sharing that pool; Mongoose documents separate pools as one way to isolate tenant workloads. (high confidence)

Node.js maxPoolSize is a per-pool bound, not a global application socket limit: each MongoClient has per-server pools and additional monitoring connections. Capacity planning must account for clients, servers and processes. (low confidence)

Mongoose useDb can share a pool across tenant databases, while separate connections can provide separate pools. Shared pools simplify management but allow one tenant's slow operations to delay another tenant. (low confidence)

Under the ordinary retryable-writes protocol, drivers attach a logical session ID and transaction number to supported writes so the server can recognize a retry. This protocol is distinct from issuing a new application-level write after an ambiguous failure. (high confidence)

Pool telemetry can distinguish checkout waiting from connection establishment or pool clearing: CMAP defines checkout-started, checkout-failed and checked-out events, including elapsed duration and failure reasons such as timeout or connectionError. (low confidence)

Slow operations can occupy pooled connections and delay other requests. Mongoose documents one operation per socket; AWS describes new requests waiting when all pool connections are busy. Tune long-running queries and pool capacity together instead of assuming a larger pool fixes server-side latency. (medium confidence)

AWS announced retryable-write support for Amazon DocumentDB engine 8.0.2 on September 28, 2026; earlier engines still require disabling it. MongoDB-compatible connection advice must therefore be scoped to the target engine rather than treating retryWrites=false as universal. This is a compatibility boundary, not a claim about MongoDB Server. (high confidence) (verified as of 2026-09-28)

MongoDB drivers are language-specific client libraries. MongoDB uses shared specifications and YAML conformance tests to align protocol behavior while retaining language-specific APIs and concurrency models. (low confidence)

Connection establishment, pool checkout, and server selection are separate timeout stages. The C# connection guide distinguishes ConnectTimeout and WaitQueueTimeout; AWS describes ServerSelectionTimeoutMS as the wait to find an eligible server. Diagnose the exhausted stage before changing a timeout. (medium confidence)

The retryable-writes specification excludes standalone servers and multi-document update/delete statements from the ordinary retryable-write protocol. Bulk eligibility is assessed for each command after ordering and batch splitting; a bulk API call is not automatically wholly retryable. (low confidence)

The accepted Client Backpressure specification adds a separate overload retry policy that can include commands outside ordinary read/write retry eligibility. It applies backoff and a bounded adaptive retry count. An application must verify its actual driver implementation before relying on these specified behaviors. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-27)

The CMAP specification standardizes connection-pool configuration, checkout/checkin, pool clearing, and monitoring events across implementing drivers; Mongoose delegates most connection options to the underlying MongoDB Node.js driver. (high confidence)

maxPoolSize limits connections associated with a pool, while maxConnecting limits concurrent connection establishment. These controls address different bottlenecks; reaching either can make checkout wait. (high confidence)

Mongoose buffers model calls before connection establishment, and bufferCommands is a Mongoose-specific option that is not passed to the native driver. A stalled buffered operation therefore requires checking wrapper initialization before attributing it to a driver defect. (low confidence)

The ordinary MongoDB retryable-writes policy excludes updateMany, deleteMany, unacknowledged writes, and individual writes inside transactions. Commit and abort have separate retry handling; bulk eligibility is evaluated for each command after batching. (low confidence)

Application-level retries need their own idempotency design: repeating a fresh $inc update can increment twice, whereas setting the same field value avoids that particular duplication. Driver retryable writes deduplicate retries carrying the same protocol identifiers; they do not make arbitrary new business operations idempotent. (high confidence)

MongoDB's client-backpressure specification defines a separate retry policy for errors carrying both RetryableError and SystemOverloadedError. It can cover commands excluded by ordinary retryable-writes rules and requires jittered exponential backoff; the specification alone does not establish support in every released driver. (high confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-27)
